idiom_name: deduplication key + atomic claim in a seen-store, wrapped around the handler
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: choose a stable message identity (producer-assigned message id or business idempotency key), keep a shared store of claimed keys with a retention window, and make the check-and-claim a single atomic step - insert into a unique key set, insert a row under a unique constraint, or set-if-absent. Commit the claim record together with the business effects; where that is impossible, record in-progress then completed states and reconcile stale entries before acknowledging. Absorb (acknowledge without reprocessing) a failed claim, and dead-letter a recurring key whose content differs instead of dropping it silently.
code_sketch:
key = message.idempotency_key or message.headers['message-id']
if not store.claim(key, ttl=REDELIVERY_WINDOW):   # atomic insert-if-absent
    acknowledge(message); return                    # duplicate: absorb, do not reprocess
with transaction():
    write_claim(key)
    apply_business_effects(message)
acknowledge(message)
pitfalls: Deriving the key from delivery metadata (receive count, timestamp, broker delivery tag) makes every redelivery look like a new message.
Writing the claim in a separate step from the side effects leaves a crash window that reprocesses on redelivery.
Retention shorter than the maximum redelivery window silently reopens duplicate processing.

Wrong move: treat every repeated key as a duplicate regardless of payload -> a reused key with changed content silently loses legitimate work -> instead compare a stable request fingerprint and dead-letter plus alert on mismatch.
